prompt: Order the sections of a 2-minute Loom video proposal for a prospect who wants an AI customer-support assistant, first to last.

task.prompt: Order the sections of a 2-minute Loom video proposal for a prospect who wants an AI customer-support assistant, first to last.

items.label: Show a similar assistant you built, on screen, for 30-40 seconds
Sketch how it would work for them and one key question
Ask for a short call and say how to book it
Greet them by name and say what you looked at (their website and support page)
Name the problem you noticed on their site, in their terms

task.explanation: Personal hook, their problem, proof, tailored idea, then a single clear next step.

prompt: Mark the problems in this plan for a Loom video proposal.

task.prompt: Mark the problems in this plan for a Loom video proposal.

segments.text: Open the video on the prospect's own website so they recognise it instantly.
Spend the first three minutes on the agency's history and team photos.
segments.issue: The opening must be about the prospect; a long intro loses viewers before the point.

segments.text: Keep the whole video around two minutes.
Record one generic video and send it to every prospect this month.
segments.issue: A generic video removes the personalisation that makes Loom proposals work.

segments.text: Show one relevant case study on screen rather than a list of ten.
End with a clear ask: a 15-minute call, with the booking link under the video.
Use a thumbnail with the prospect's site visible so the email preview is personal.
Leave background tabs with other clients' data visible while recording.
segments.issue: Exposes other clients' information; close unrelated tabs before recording.

prompt: An inbound lead from a fitness-studio chain filled in a form: 'Want a booking app. Can you send info?' You decide to reply with a short Loom.

task.prompt: An inbound lead from a fitness-studio chain filled in a form: 'Want a booking app. Can you send info?' You decide to reply with a short Loom.

steps.question: What should the video show first?
options: A full price list
Code from a past project
Your agency's pitch deck
Their current booking flow on their website, and where it creates friction
steps.explanation: Starting on their own site proves you looked and frames the problem.

steps.question: What should the email around the video say?
options: Nothing, just the link
A full proposal with fixed price
One line on what the video covers and a link to book a call
A request that they watch it twice
steps.explanation: A short context line raises the chance they click; the video does the persuasion and the email gives the next step.

prompt: You compared text-only proposals with Loom proposals over a quarter. Calculate the call-booking rate (%) and the win rate (%) for each.

task.prompt: You compared text-only proposals with Loom proposals over a quarter. Calculate the call-booking rate (%) and the win rate (%) for each.

prompt: A rep spends 20 minutes on each Loom proposal and 8 minutes on each text proposal. Using the rates below, calculate the minutes of rep time per win for each approach.

task.prompt: A rep spends 20 minutes on each Loom proposal and 8 minutes on each text proposal. Using the rates below, calculate the minutes of rep time per win for each approach.
task.explanation: Text: 8 / 0.025 = 320 minutes per win. Loom: 20 / 0.10 = 200 minutes per win. Loom costs more per proposal but less per win.

prompt: Your Loom proposals get high view counts but few replies. Loom shows most viewers stop watching around 50 seconds into 4-minute videos.

task.prompt: Your Loom proposals get high view counts but few replies. Loom shows most viewers stop watching around 50 seconds into 4-minute videos.

steps.question: What does the drop-off suggest?
options: The thumbnail is wrong
The links are broken
Videos are too long and the key point comes too late
Prospects are not interested in video at all
steps.explanation: Viewers start watching but leave early, so the content order and length are the issue.

steps.question: What change do you make?
options: Add background music
Send the same video twice
Make videos longer with more detail
Cut to about 2 minutes and put the prospect's problem and the ask in the first 30 seconds
steps.explanation: Front-load what matters and shorten the video so the ask is seen.

prompt: What most makes a Loom proposal outperform a text proposal?

options: Visible personalisation: showing the prospect's own product or site and talking about their problem
Higher video resolution
A longer running time
Background music and animations
mcq.explanation: Proof that you looked at their business, delivered in a human voice, is what drives replies.

prompt: When is a Loom video proposal NOT worth the extra time?

options: For a low-value or poor-fit lead where a short text reply is enough
For a high-value inbound lead
When the prospect has a website you can show
When you have a relevant case study to show on screen
mcq.explanation: Video takes more time per lead, so save it for leads where fit and value justify it.

prompt: A prospect watched your Loom twice and shared it with a colleague, but has not replied. What is the best follow-up?

options: Send the same video again
Wait a month before following up
Ask why they have not replied yet
A short note referencing the colleague's likely question and offering a call with both
mcq.explanation: Engagement signals a second stakeholder is involved; a follow-up that includes them moves the deal forward.
